butir.teks: The duties of the guiding teacher

Know that a person has four states with regard to his knowledge, like his state in acquiring wealth, for the owner of wealth has a state of gaining, so he is an earner; a state of saving what he has earned, so through it he is free of the need to ask; a state of spending on himself, so he benefits; and a state of giving to others, so through it he is generous and bountiful, and this is the noblest of his states.

So too knowledge is acquired as wealth is acquired. It has a state of seeking and earning; a state of attainment that frees one from asking; a state of gaining insight (istibsar), which is reflecting on what has been attained and enjoying it; and a state of giving insight (tabsir), which is the noblest of the states. Whoever knows, acts, and teaches is the one who is called great in the kingdom of the heavens, for he is like the sun that gives light to others while shining in itself, and like musk that perfumes others while being fragrant itself.

As for the one who teaches and does not act on it, he is like the notebook that benefits others while empty of knowledge, like the whetstone that sharpens others and does not cut, like the needle that clothes others while bare, and like the wick of the lamp that gives light to others while it burns, as has been said:
It is nothing but a wick that was lit ... giving light to the people while it burns.
Whenever he occupies himself with teaching, he has taken on a great matter and a weighty danger, so let him keep its proper conduct and its duties.

The first duty: compassion towards the learners, and that he treat them as he would his own sons. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "I am to you only like a father to his child." (١) This is by aiming to rescue them from the Fire of the Hereafter, which is more important than parents rescuing their child from the fire of this world. For that reason the right of the teacher became greater than the right of the parents, for the father is the cause of present existence and perishing life, while the teacher is the cause of lasting life.

Were it not for the teacher, what was obtained from the father's side would be driven to everlasting destruction. The teacher is only the one who provides everlasting life in the Hereafter, I mean the teacher of the sciences of the Hereafter, or the sciences

of this world with the intention of the Hereafter, not with the intention of this world. As for teaching with the intention of this world, it is destruction and causing destruction; we seek refuge in Allah from it.

Just as it is the right of the sons of one man to love one another and to help one another in all aims, so too it is the right of the students of one man to love one another and be affectionate to one another. It can be only so if their aim is the Hereafter, and there can be only mutual envy and hatred if their aim is this world.
For the scholars and the sons of the Hereafter are travellers to Allah Most High, walking the road to Him from this world, and its years and months are the stages of the road.

Companionship on the road among those travelling to cities is a cause of affection and love, so how much more the journey to the highest Firdaws and companionship on the way to it! There is no narrowness in the happiness of the Hereafter, and for that reason there is no dispute among the sons of the Hereafter; and there is no breadth in the happiness of this world, and for that reason it is never free from the narrowness of crowding.

Those who incline to seeking leadership through the sciences go outside what is required by His saying, Most High, ⟦QS 49:10⟧ and enter into what is implied by His saying, Most High, ⟦QS 43:67⟧ The second duty: that he follow the Master of the Law (peace and blessings be upon him), so he does not ask for a wage for imparting knowledge, nor does he intend by it a reward or thanks, but teaches for the sake of Allah Most High and in seeking nearness to Him. He does not see any favour for himself over them, though the favour is incumbent upon them; rather he sees the merit as theirs, since they have purified their hearts so that they draw near to Allah Most High by cultivating the sciences in them. It is like one who lends you land so that you may plant a crop in it for yourself: your benefit from it exceeds the benefit of the owner of the land, so how can you burden him with an obligation? And your reward for teaching is greater than the reward of the learner with Allah Most High, and were it not for the learner you would not have attained this reward. So do not seek the wage except from Allah Most High, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says, ⟦QS 11:29⟧ For wealth and what is in this world is a servant of the body, and the body is the mount and riding beast of the self, and the one served is knowledge, for by it is the nobility of the self.

In sum, the merit and the favour belong to the teacher. So look how the matter of religion has come to a people who claim that their aim is to draw near to Allah Most High through what they are engaged in of the knowledge of jurisprudence (fiqh) and theology (kalam) and teaching them and other subjects. For they spend wealth and status and bear all kinds of humiliation in serving the sultans in order to obtain stipends, and if they left that, they would be left and no one would come to them. Then the teacher expects the learner to stand up for him in every misfortune, to support his ally, to be hostile to his enemy, to rise openly for him in his needs, and to be pressed into service before him in his wants; and if the learner falls short in his right, the teacher rises against him and becomes one of his most hostile enemies. How vile is a scholar who is content for himself with this rank, then rejoices in it, then is not ashamed to say, "My aim in teaching is to spread knowledge, to draw near to Allah Most High and to support His religion." So look at the signs until you see the kinds of delusion.

The third duty: that he not leave out any advice to the learner. That is by preventing him from aspiring to a rank before he deserves it, and from busying himself with an obscure knowledge before finishing the clear one; then alerting him that the aim of seeking the sciences is nearness to Allah Most High, not leadership, boasting, and rivalry; and putting first the making of that appear ugly in his self as far as possible, for what a wicked scholar reforms is no more than what he corrupts. If he knows from his inner state that he seeks knowledge only for this world, he looks at the knowledge he seeks. If it is the knowledge of disagreement in jurisprudence, disputation in theology, and fatwas in disputes and rulings, he prevents him from it, for these sciences are not among the sciences of the Hereafter, nor among the sciences about which it was said, "We learned knowledge for other than Allah, but knowledge refused to be anything except for Allah." That is only the knowledge of exegesis (tafsir), the knowledge of hadith, and what the earlier generations used to occupy themselves with of the knowledge of the Hereafter and knowing the character traits of the self and how to refine it. If the student learns it and intends this world by it, there is no harm in leaving him be, for it bears fruit in him as a craving for preaching and gaining a following. But he may awaken in the course of the matter or at its end, since in it are the sciences that instil fear of Allah Most High, belittle this world, and magnify the Hereafter. And that
is likely to lead to what is right in the Hereafter, until he is admonished by what he admonishes others with.

The love of acceptance and status serves as the grain that is scattered around the trap to catch birds with it. Allah has done the same with His servants, for He made appetite so that through it creation reach the continuation of offspring.

He also created the love of status to be a cause of reviving the sciences. This is to be expected in these sciences. As for pure disagreements, the disputations of theology, and knowledge of strange sub-issues, devoting oneself exclusively to them while turning away from others increases nothing but hardness of heart, heedlessness of Allah Most High, persistence in misguidance, and seeking status, except for one whom Allah Most High reaches with His mercy or who mixes other religious sciences with it.

There is no proof of this like experience and observation. So look, take heed, and gain insight, so that you witness the realisation of that among the servants and in the lands. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

Sufyan ath-Thawri (may Allah have mercy on him) was once seen sorrowful, and it was said to him, "What is the matter with you?" He said, "We have become a trading place for the sons of this world: one of them attaches himself to us, until when he has learned, he is made a judge, or a governor, or a steward (qahraman)."
